title: Choosing Models, Deployments and Parameters

header.html: Identify an appropriate AI model, based on capabilities; Identify appropriate model deployment options and configuration parameters
the official AI-901 study guide, skills measured as of April 15, 2026

html:
1The model catalog

Microsoft Foundry has a model catalog with more than 10,000 models from Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and others. [Verify live] The catalog has two categories:

Category Who hosts and sells it Why you pick it
Foundry Models sold by Azure Microsoft hosts and sells them under Microsoft Product Terms; billed through Azure Deep Azure integration, guaranteed support, enterprise service levels
Foundry Models from partners and community Partners and the community; billed through the Azure Marketplace Specialized use cases and the newest ideas

2Choose a model by capability

Pick the model whose capability matches the task, then weigh cost and speed.

Need Kind of model Notes
General chat, writing, summarizing, coding Large language model (LLM) Most capable, most costly
Simple, high-volume, low-cost or fast tasks Small language model (SLM) Cheaper and faster, less general
Hard multi-step problems: math, logic, planning Reasoning model Thinks before answering; slower; some settings are not supported
Understand images (and sometimes audio) in prompts Multimodal model Accepts more than text
Create images from a text description Image-generation model Output is an image
Turn text into vectors for semantic search Embedding model Output is numbers, not text
Speech to text or text to speech Speech model or Azure Speech Module 5 and 10

Exam tip

. The exam asks "which kind of model" more than "which model name". Words to match: reasoning = multi-step logic; multimodal = images or audio in; embedding = similarity search; image generation = create pictures; SLM = cheap and fast.

3Deployment options

Before you use a model you deploy it. The deployment type decides where it runs, how you pay and how much traffic it can take.

Category Deployment types Meaning
Standard (pay per token) Global Standard, Data Zone Standard, Standard You pay for the tokens you use. Global Standard can run in any Azure region and has the highest quota; Data Zone keeps processing in a data zone (US, EU or APAC); Standard stays within one Azure geography
Provisioned (reserved capacity) Global, Data Zone and Regional Provisioned You reserve capacity (throughput units) for steady, predictable, high volume
Batch (asynchronous) Global and Data Zone Batch Discounted processing of large jobs that can wait (up to about 24 hours; Global Batch is described with a 50% discount)
Developer Developer tier Evaluating fine-tuned models only: 24-hour lifetime, no service level agreement

[Verify live] for current names, discounts and limits.

Exam tip

. "Start simple, pay per use" → Global Standard. "Predictable high volume, reserved capacity" → provisioned. "Large job, not urgent, cheaper" → batch. "Data must stay in the EU" → a Data Zone or regional type.

4Configuration parameters

When you call a model you can set parameters that change how it answers.

Parameter What it does Typical use
temperature Controls randomness. The range is 0 to 2. Low (for example 0.2) gives focused, predictable answers; high (for example 0.7 or more) gives more varied, creative answers Low for facts and extraction; higher for ideas and stories
top_p Another way to control randomness: the model picks only from the most likely tokens that add up to this probability. It is similar to temperature Change temperature or top_p, not both
max tokens (max_completion_tokens for newer models) The maximum number of tokens the model may generate in the answer Cap cost and length; set it high enough for the expected answer or the reply is cut off (finish reason "length")
  • Reasoning models use max_completion_tokens instead of max_tokens, and do not support temperature, top_p or the penalty parameters.
  • The system message (module 6) is not a number but also shapes the answer.

Exam tip

. "More creative" → raise temperature. "Same answer every time, factual" → lower temperature. "Reply stops in the middle" → raise max tokens. "Reasoning model" → no temperature setting.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors needs a model that can describe photos that customers upload. Which kind of model fits?

  • AAn embedding model
  • BA text-only small model
  • CA multimodal model
  • DA speech model
Show the answer

Answer: C. A multimodal model accepts images (and sometimes audio) as part of the prompt.

S2A team needs a very fast, low-cost model for simple labeling at high volume. Which kind of model fits best?

  • AA reasoning model
  • BAn image-generation model
  • CA provisioned throughput of the largest model only
  • DA small language model
Show the answer

Answer: D. Small language models are cheaper and faster and are enough for focused tasks.

S3A product team wants product descriptions that vary and sound creative. Which setting change helps?

  • ALower the temperature to 0
  • BLower max tokens to 1
  • CRemove the system message
  • DRaise the temperature
Show the answer

Answer: D. A higher temperature gives more varied and creative output.

S4A company wants to keep its prompts and responses processed in the EU. Which deployment idea fits?

  • AA Data Zone deployment for the EU
  • BThe Developer tier for evaluation
  • CA random Global deployment in any region
  • DBatch only for overnight jobs
Show the answer

Answer: A. Data Zone deployment types keep processing inside a data zone such as the EU.

S5A reply from the model stops in the middle of a sentence and the finish reason is "length". What should be checked?

  • AThe temperature setting of the model
  • BThe max tokens (max_completion_tokens) setting
  • CThe model catalog category of the deployment
  • DThe name of the Azure subscription
Show the answer

Answer: B. The output hit the token limit, so the maximum must be raised.

S6A team plans a large overnight job that is not urgent and wants a lower price. Which deployment category fits?

  • ABatch
  • BDeveloper tier
  • CProvisioned only
  • DInteractive chat playground
Show the answer

Answer: A. Batch processes large jobs asynchronously at a discount.

5.2 Recall questions

R1Which two categories does the Foundry model catalog have?

Show the answer

Foundry Models sold by Azure, and Foundry Models from partners and community.

R2Which deployment type is the usual starting point?

Show the answer

Global Standard.

R3What does a low temperature do?

Show the answer

Gives more focused, predictable answers.

R4Which two settings should you not change together?

Show the answer

Temperature and top_p.

R5What do reasoning models use instead of max_tokens?

Show the answer

max_completion_tokens.

R6Which kind of model creates vectors for similarity search?

Show the answer

An embedding model.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Catalog 10,000+ models; sold by Azure vs partners and community
Model kinds LLM, SLM, reasoning, multimodal, image generation, embedding
Deployment standard (pay per token, Global Standard first), provisioned (reserved), batch (discounted, asynchronous), developer (evaluation only)
Data location Global = any region; Data Zone = US, EU or APAC; Standard and Regional = one geography
Parameters temperature 0 to 2 (low focused, high varied); top_p similar; max tokens caps the answer
Reasoning models max_completion_tokens; no temperature, top_p
